value.rationale: The exact semi-open Glauber theta correlation is significantly less convenient than its proposed erf quotient. The derived bound provides an actionable, uniform-in-separation error budget throughout the physically recommended early finite-size window, with the best possible exponential scale; at \(t\le N^2/8\) it certifies a strict absolute error below \(0.00470\) absolute error across the entire chain. It also identifies the qualitatively erroneous time-integrated inference generated by invalid long-time extrapolation, even though the exact finite system is spectrally gapped. Both domain certification and the limit of extrapolation are naturally motivated by the source's use of a finite-size scaling shortcut. No downstream general theorem is asserted.
